word.name: set-has-a-parent
word.title: Set Has A Parent
word.description: Every set is directly under at least one superset or set, so some class thread reaches it and its elements.

graphRule.name: set-has-a-parent
graphRule.says: every set is directly under at least one superset or set, so some class thread reaches it and its elements. A superset is exempt: its concept's header holds it in its class thread. Only a superset or a set counts as a parent, so an element an old route put above a set doesn't. And only a node with an address, its `uuid`, is judged as a set or counted as a parent: the trust pipeline's card sets are labelled `Set` but have no address, so they are neither (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0028 Amendment 3).
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the class threads' sets.
graphRule.refusesOrReports: it refuses the write, before anything changes: `last-parent` (409) when taking a set out from under a parent would leave it under no other superset or set. The refusal names that parent and says how to go on: link the set under another parent first, or delete it once it is empty (`graph delete-set`, A10.17). Taking out a link that isn't there is a repeat, not a refusal.
graphRule.check: the same `violations` over a set of sets, with no parent to leave, names each set under no superset or set. `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over the graph's sets, those with an address, so it reports none of the trust pipeline's card sets. Today's `POST /api/normalize/delete-relationship` doesn't check for a set's last parent, so it can leave one.
graphRule.repair: `graph link-set` gives a set with no parent one; `graph delete-set` (A10.17) deletes it once it is empty.
graphRule.enforcedBy: the guard of `graph unlink-set`, which runs the rule again after its write, inside the same transaction. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/set-has-a-parent.js`, and what it reads with is in `src/operations/catalog/graph/_sets.js`. Built in story graph-operations-first-slice #28 (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0028).

code.summary: Every set is directly under at least one superset or set; a superset is exempt, since its concept's header holds it in its class thread.

refusals.when: Taking the link out would leave the set under no superset or set, so no class thread would reach it or its elements
